lie_deviation_conversion_rule.note: No officially sourced numeric conversion (e.g. '1 degree of lie = X yards deviation') found in reliable sources during this session. Only qualitative guidance found: upright lie tends to promote left start (right-handed golfer), flat lie tends to promote right start.

lie_board_impact_tape_interpretation.note: No standardized numeric interpretation (e.g. mm heel/toe offset to degrees) found from a reliable manufacturer source during this session. Qualitative rule only: heel-side impact mark suggests lie too upright (needs flattening); toe-side impact mark suggests lie too flat (needs uprighting).

steps: Stand on a hard, flat surface (not carpet)
Wear flat shoes (athletic shoes, not spiked golf shoes; sole max ~1.5 in)
Stand naturally upright, no slouching or stretching
Let arms hang relaxed at sides
Measure from the wrist crease of the lead hand (left hand for right-handed golfer) straight down to the floor
Repeat 2-3 times, use most consistent value
